title: Epidemiology, treatment and outcomes of antimicrobial-resistant infections in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients
authors: Estela Carvalho de Sousa et al.
one_line_summary: Multidrug-resistant bacterial infections cause high morbidity in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients, but novel beta-lactams, optimized daptomycin dosing, and stewardship strategies provide effective targeted treatment options.
key_pearls: **Ceftolozane-tazobactam** is the preferred agent for **difficult-to-treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa (DTR-PA)** in HCT recipients, with combination therapy reserved for selected severe cases.

**Ceftazidime-avibactam** is the primary first-line option for **KPC-producing** and **OXA-48-producing** Enterobacterales, **significantly** reducing **mortality** when initiated within **48 hours**.
For **metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL)-producing** Enterobacterales, combination therapy with **ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam** or **cefiderocol** represents the preferred approach.
Higher **daptomycin** doses of **8–12 mg/kg/day** optimize PK/PD target attainment and **survival** in **VRE** and **MRSA** bloodstream infections.
Short-course antibiotic regimens (**7–11 days**) for Gram-negative bloodstream infections appear safe after neutrophil recovery and help prevent resistance selection.
population: Hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HCT) recipients and patients with hematological malignancies (HM)

sections.heading: Epidemiology of Resistant Bacterial Infections in HCT Recipients
sections.content:
- Bloodstream infections (**BSI**) occur in approximately **30%** of patients with hematological malignancies (**HM**) or undergoing **HCT**, with a balance of Gram-positive (**51%**) and Gram-negative (**42%**) species.
- Median extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (**ESBL**) / third-generation cephalosporin resistance (**3GCR**) reaches **30%** (range **6–51%**) in European centers.
- Carbapenem resistance (**CR**) affects **13%** of overall Enterobacterales and **38%** of **Klebsiella pneumoniae** BSI in European cohorts, with higher global pooled rates of **21%** in Enterobacterales and **30%** in **Pseudomonas aeruginosa**.
- Methicillin-resistant **Staphylococcus aureus** (**MRSA**) pooled prevalence is **43%**, while vancomycin-resistant **Enterococcus** (**VRE**) prevalence is **41%** among enterococcal isolates globally.
- Marked geographical variability exists, with higher carbapenem resistance in South-Eastern Europe and South Africa, and higher **VRE** rates reported in the U.S.
section_pearls: Carbapenem resistance rates reach **38%** among **K. pneumoniae** isolates in European HM/HCT cohorts.
Prior antibiotic exposures during pre-engraftment neutropenia significantly drive resistant bacterial acquisition.

sections.heading: Treatment of Difficult-to-Treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa
sections.content:
- **Difficult-to-treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa** (**DTR-PA**) BSI carries 30-day **mortality** rates up to **38%**, with **33.8%** presenting in septic shock.
- **Ceftolozane-tazobactam** is the preferred agent for **DTR-PA**, demonstrating **superior** clinical success compared to **ceftazidime-avibactam** in the **CACTUS** study (*aOR 2.07*), particularly in pneumonia.
- Treatment-emergent resistance occurs in **22–23%** of initially susceptible **P. aeruginosa** isolates during therapy with novel beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitors.
- **Cefiderocol** is an effective alternative reserved for **MBL-producing** **P. aeruginosa** (e.g., **VIM** producers), achieving **28-day cure rates** of **81%** in immunocompromised patients.
- **ECIL-10** guidelines support combination therapy (novel beta-lactam plus an aminoglycoside, fluoroquinolone, or fosfomycin) for **DTR-PA** in **critically** ill neutropenic patients or uncontrolled infection sources.
section_pearls: Treatment-emergent resistance develops in over **20%** of **P. aeruginosa** isolates undergoing novel beta-lactam therapy.

sections.heading: Management of Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales
sections.content:
- **Ceftazidime-avibactam** initiated within **48 hours** of CRE BSI onset reduces **30-day mortality** to **16.7%**, compared to **50.0%** when used as second-line therapy.
- For **KPC** and **OXA-48** producers, **ECIL-10** gives the highest recommendation to **ceftazidime-avibactam**, followed by **meropenem-vaborbactam**, **imipenem-relebactam**, and **cefiderocol**.
- For **MBL-producing Enterobacterales** (e.g., **NDM**, **VIM**), combination therapy with **ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam** is preferred over **cefiderocol** monotherapy due to concerns over emergent **cefiderocol** resistance in **NDM** strains.
- The randomized **ASSEMBLE** phase 3 trial confirmed efficacy of **aztreonam-avibactam** in **MBL-producing** Gram-negative infections with a low 28-day **mortality** of **8%** (**1/12**).
section_pearls: Delaying **ceftazidime-avibactam** beyond **48 hours** in CRE BSI increases 30-day mortality threefold.
**Aztreonam** plus **ceftazidime-avibactam** is the primary regimen for **MBL-producing** Enterobacterales.

sections.heading: Management of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Infections
sections.content:
- **Stenotrophomonas maltophilia** causes **2.2–5%** of post-HCT infections, carrying pre-engraftment **mortality** up to **60%** due to intrinsic resistance to standard empiric carbapenems.
- Application of clinical risk tools like **StenoScore2** (sensitivity **86%**, specificity **76%**) aids in reducing treatment delays, which currently average **3 days**.
- **Cefiderocol** achieves **62–70%** clinical cure rates and **30-day mortality** of **30–37%** in **S. maltophilia** infections.
- Resistance to frontline agents reaches **15.1%** for **levofloxacin** and **14.6%** for **trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole** (**TMP-SMX**).
- **ECIL-10** recommends combination therapy with **two active agents** (including **TMP-SMX** as one component if feasible) until clinical improvement and susceptibility confirmation allow de-escalation.
section_pearls: Always use combination therapy (including **TMP-SMX**) initially for **S. maltophilia** in HCT recipients.
Intrinsic resistance to carbapenems delays active therapy for **S. maltophilia** by a median of **3 days**.

sections.heading: Treatment of Resistant Gram-Positive Infections
sections.content:
- **VRE** BSI in HCT recipients serves as a marker for advanced disease and severe underlying morbidity, with 100-day overall **mortality** reported at **83–100%**.
- **Daptomycin** at high doses (**8–12 mg/kg/day**) demonstrates **superior** 30-day **survival** in **VRE BSI** compared to non-daptomycin regimens (**linezolid** or **tigecycline**).
- **Tigecycline-based** regimens for **VRE BSI** are independently associated with increased 30-day **mortality**.
- Acquired **daptomycin resistance** is increasingly recognized in **Enterococcus faecium** after prior daptomycin exposure in young, heavily treated HCT recipients.
- Long-acting lipoglycopeptides (**dalbavancin**, **oritavancin**) and novel 5th-generation cephalosporins (**ceftobiprole**) provide alternative outpatient and inpatient strategies for **MRSA** and **VRE**.
section_pearls: Avoid **tigecycline** for **VRE BSI** due to documented increased mortality.
High-dose **daptomycin** (**8–12 mg/kg/day**) improves target attainment and survival in enterococcal BSI.

sections.heading: Antimicrobial Stewardship and Duration of Therapy
sections.content:
- Short-course antibiotic therapy (**7–11 days**) for **P. aeruginosa** and Enterobacterales BSI is non-**inferior** to prolonged courses (**12–21 days**) in high-risk neutropenic hematology patients.
- Treatment discontinuation in Gram-negative BSI should occur only after **neutrophil recovery** or an initial neutrophil rise.
- De-escalation and stewardship strategies reduce overall carbapenem exposure, successfully curbing the incidence of **carbapenem-resistant** Gram-negative BSI over long-term follow-up.
section_pearls: Gram-negative BSI therapy can be safely shortened to **7 days** once neutropenia resolves.
Stewardship programs halting routine fluoroquinolone prophylaxis reduce local carbapenem resistance rates.

strengths_limitations:
- **Strengths**: Synthesizes recent multicenter observational data and clinical trial evidence specifically focused on immunocompromised, HM, and HCT populations; offers granular treatment recommendations aligned with ECIL-10, IDSA, and ESCMID guidelines.
- **Limitations**: Sparse randomized controlled trial data exclusively enrolling HCT recipients; observational comparative studies carry inherent selection and immortal time biases; **significant** regional variation in resistance mechanisms limits global extrapolation of specific empiric regimens.
